subject: System Design
title: Secondary Indexes in Partitioned Systems
description: A fast breakdown of Secondary Indexes in Partitioned Systems for builders.

hook.text: Data is partitioned by user ID. A query asks for all users in New York. The index must span all partitions.

buildup.text: Local indexes live on each partition. A query must scatter to all partitions and gather results.

discovery.text: Global indexes are partitioned separately by the indexed value. One query hits one index partition.

twist.text: Global indexes must be updated across partitions on every write. Async updates mean stale index results.

climax.text: Local indexes are write-efficient but read-expensive. Global indexes are the opposite. Pick your trade-off.

punchline.text: Local indexes: fast writes. Global indexes: fast reads.

quiz.question: What is the downside of local secondary indexes in partitioned systems?
options: Queries must scatter across all partitions
